para.text: This example is based on one of the PEST examples for MODFLOW 6:
. That in turn is based on the MODFLOW-2005

has a lake near the north and a stream at the south both of which are simulated using specified head boundaries. Flow is from north to south. There is a disposal pond in the north that is as source of solute. Further south, there are two water supply wells that might receive some of the solute from the disposal pond. This example will take the completed version of the MODFLOW 6 model and add a Particle Transport (PRT) model. After running the PRT model, the particle tracks will be plotted. Next we will change the model to use the estimated hydraulic conductiviites that were already imported into the ModelMuse file and plot the new particle tracks to see how they have changed.

Next the model will be changed to use a Voronoi mesh. Updated hydraulic conductivities can be estimated using PEST. The tracks generated by the Particle Transport model will be plotted using the original uniform hydraulic conductivities and then with the updated hydraulic conductivities. Plotting the new particle tracks will show how changing the hydraulic conductivity can change the flow of water.
The goals of this exercise are:

li.text: Illustrate how to create a Particle Transport (PRT) model and plot its results.
Illustrate how to create a Voronoi mesh using VOROGRIDGEN.
